purpose: Prevent accidental house style from emerging because generated or legacy prose is frequent in the corpus.

states.canonical: Ratified language resource or terminology source for new generation.
states.accepted: Reviewed content accepted for its owning use; eligible as an exemplar only inside that scope.
states.generatedDraft: Machine-produced text not yet accepted; never a house-style authority.
states.quotedSource: Source voice preserved for evidence; not house prose.
states.deprecated: Retained for provenance but excluded from new canonical generation.

rules: Frequency does not promote a resource to canonical.
A repeated defect is evidence for a generator/template investigation, not a style vote.
Training, retrieval, prompting, and few-shot selection prefer canonical language fibers and reviewed exemplars over raw nearest-neighbor prose.
Quoted source can inform facts or voice attribution but cannot silently become 561 house style.
When canonicality is unknown, keep it explicit instead of inventing acceptance.

currentEvidence.pattern: maintains knowledge and practices for this service domain
currentEvidence.disposition: known systemic scaffold debt; exclude from exemplars

currentEvidence.pattern: Its material is organized by artifact role under content/; specialized subdomains continue under services/.
